prompt: Make a small web app for signing up for our workshop. There are 20 seats; people enter their name and email and get a seat.

WS1.reason: Signups are stored separately in each page's memory, with no shared atomic seat limit.

WS2.reason: Duplicate emails are checked only within one page instance, so the same email can register in another instance.

WS3.reason: The attendee list displays registered participants' names and email addresses to anyone viewing that page instance.

WS1.reason: The code uses in-memory state without any locking or atomic operations, so simultaneous sign-ups could exceed 20 seats due to race conditions.

WS2.reason: The code checks for existing emails with emailExists() before adding a new attendee, preventing duplicate email registrations.

WS3.reason: The attendee list is rendered publicly in the HTML and visible to all visitors, exposing names and email addresses.

WS1.reason: State lives only in each browser's memory with no server, so there is no shared seat count or atomic booking; each visitor has their own 20 seats.

WS2.reason: The emailExists check rejects a duplicate email case-insensitively, but only within the single in-memory page session.

WS3.reason: The page renders a public attendee list showing every name and email to anyone viewing it.
